messages:
Anya: Heads-up — bringing up the new reranker (rbk-3b-v2) across hosted/dedicated/private for a quick quality smoke.
Kevin: Nice. primary checks?
Anya: NDCG@10, MRR@5, and per-query variance. Also compare int8 vs fp16 kernels.
Priya: Do we have a consistent sample? candidate pool and query doc formatting must be identical across runs.
Johan: I noticed kernel selection changes output on long docs before — can bias ranking.
Anya: Exactly. For this run I pinned tokenizer and candidate order. command I used:
```bash
./eval_runner --model rbk-3b-v2 --backend hosted,dedicated,private \
  --quant int8,fp16 --cohort sample_20k --seed 42 --keep-order
```
Priya: Nice. what's the sampling protocol?
Anya: stratified by query length and intent label (informational/transactional). 20k queries total, same candidate set for each query.
Kevin: Quick question — how many repeats per config? seed variance can be large.
Anya: 3 seeds (42/84/128) for each backend+quant combo.
Johan: Please record per-query delta distributions, not just aggregated NDCG.
Anya: Will do. eval-bot: run queued. status: started on hosted @3099990100.
Kevin: Any early signals?
Anya: Hosted int8 shows -0.9% NDCG@10 vs fp16, MRR down 1.3%. dedicated int8 is -0.2%.
Priya: That's interesting — same model, different backends, different regression magnitude.
Johan: Could be different kernel numerics or batching order. What about top1 swaps count?
Anya: Top1 swaps (hosted int8 vs hosted fp16): 2.5% of queries. dedicated int8 vs fp16: 0.8%.
Kevin: Can we repro by forcing the same kernel selection on hosted? (if possible)
Anya: I forced kernel flags on dedicated but hosting auto-selected a different kernel. We can request a kernel pin for a test.
Priya: Also check KV cache behavior + prefix caching differences between backends — that can change attention accumulation.
Anya: Good call. I'll add a run with cache disabled.
Anya: eval-bot: hosted run completed @3099990220. pushed logs to s3://redwood-evals/rbk3b/v2/3099990000/hosted/int8/
Kevin: Can you share quick sample where rank order flipped?
Anya: Dropped a few examples in thread: query ids 1223, 4789, 9031. snippet:
```
query: "best way to shuffle dataset in streaming"
candidate A (fp16): doc about tf.data shuffle -> score 0.84
candidate B (int8): doc about seed-based shuffle -> score 0.86
```
Priya: Those look borderline ties. Could be tiny logits shifts amplified by softmax.
Johan: If ties are frequent, consider small temperature tweak or tiebreaker policy at serving.
Anya: Agreed. We'll log score margins distribution.
Kevin: How about dataset provenance? Any chance candidate normalization differed (html vs plain text)?
Anya: We normalized strip_html and canonicalized whitespace for all runs. same pipeline.
Priya: For private backend, network timeouts can truncate streams — ensure full sequence delivered to scorer.
Anya: Private run finished @3099990300 — int8 delta ~ -0.25% NDCG.
Johan: So dedicated = private ~ small delta, hosted worse. suggests hosted kernel selection + micro-batching differences.
Kevin: Action items?
Anya: 1) Re-run hosted with kernel pin to match dedicated. 2) Run with cache disabled on hosted/dedicated/private. 3) Increase sample for borderline queries (those with margin <0.05) to 100k.
Priya: Also add an A/B shadow test on production traffic for 48h with canary routing.
Johan: I'll draft a short ops playbook inc. rollback thresholds (NDCG drop >0.5% or top1 swap >3%).
Anya: I'll open a GH issue with logs and sample ids and assign to infra + runtime to investigate kernel selection policy.
eval-bot: queued tasks created: #RBK3B-127 (kernel-pin test), #RBK3B-128 (cache-disabled run)
Kevin: Thanks. If kernel pin removes regression we can schedule a careful rollout.
Anya: Thanks all. I'll post results in this thread when runs complete. :rocket:
